questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: What is a PCollection?
options: An immutable, potentially distributed multiset of elements
A mutable buffer that workers append to as elements arrive
A handle to the runner's execution plan for one pipeline stage
A partitioned view over the source that is read on demand

questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: What does a PTransform do?
options: It rewrites the elements of its input PCollection in place
It consumes zero or more PCollections and produces zero or more
It declares which runner the enclosing pipeline should execute on
It materializes its input so later stages can be retried cheaply

questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: Why must key encoding be deterministic?
options: Because keys are compared as text when the runner logs pipeline metrics
Because a nondeterministic coder makes the pipeline fail to serialize
Because logically equal keys must encode identically or they group apart
Because the runner sorts keys by their encoded bytes before every shuffle

questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: When is a side input a poor choice?
options: For a lookup map that changes between one pipeline run and the next
For reference data that arrives on its own unbounded input stream
For a small table whose rows are needed by only one transform
For a multi-gigabyte dimension that must reach every worker

questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: Why can capturing a local database client inside a user function fail?
options: The function is serialized to workers and the client may not be serializable
User functions run on the driver, where the worker's credentials are absent
Any external call inside a transform forces the runner to insert a shuffle
Connections opened before submission are closed when the graph is built

questions.topic: The Beam Model: PCollections and Transforms
questions.question: Why should an error side output have an explicit sink?
options: Because a side output with no consumer is rejected when the graph is built
Because malformed records otherwise vanish with no operational visibility
Because unread side outputs accumulate in state until the worker runs out
Because the runner retries the main output until every branch is consumed

questions.question: What does a keyed shuffle primarily do?
options: It sorts each element's fields so the coder can encode them compactly
It splits the input into bundles sized for the available worker memory
It redistributes elements so that all values for a key meet in one place
It rebalances work across workers whenever one falls behind the others

questions.question: Which transform commonly requires a shuffle?
options: A Filter that drops elements failing a predicate
A Map that converts each element to a key-value pair
A ParDo that parses each element's JSON payload
A GroupByKey that gathers all values sharing a key

questions.question: Why can CombinePerKey transfer less data than grouping all raw values?
options: Workers merge partial accumulators locally before anything crosses the network
It compresses each key's values into a single encoded block before transfer
It samples the input and extrapolates the aggregate from the sampled subset
It moves the aggregation into the source so only results are ever emitted

questions.question: What is the effect of one key owning 40 percent of events?
options: The runner splits that key across workers, so throughput stays balanced
One partition becomes a straggler and may exhaust that worker's memory
The shuffle is skipped for that key and its values are combined locally
Autoscaling adds workers until each holds an equal share of the events

questions.question: How does key salting mitigate a hot key?
options: It rewrites the hot key so its elements hash into the least loaded partition
It buffers the hot key's elements and releases them once the others finish
It aggregates deterministic subkeys first, then merges the partial results
It routes the hot key to a dedicated worker sized for its share of traffic

questions.question: One join key has 100 left rows and 1000 right rows. What is the maximum pairwise output?
In Beam's four questions, what does 'what' describe?
options: The computation being applied, such as a sum, a count or a sketch
The event-time window that decides which elements are grouped
The trigger policy that decides when a pane is emitted downstream
The accumulation mode relating each pane to the ones before it

questions.question: What does 'where' describe?
options: The region and worker pool the runner schedules the job onto
The event-time window that assigns elements into groups
The sink table that each pane's output is finally written to
The partition an element occupies once the shuffle completes

questions.question: An event has event time 10:07 and arrives at 10:20. Which fixed five-minute window contains it?
What does 'how' describe?
options: How elements are encoded for transport between fused pipeline stages
How the watermark advances as the source observes event-time progress
How many panes a window may emit before its state is finally cleaned up
How successive panes accumulate, discard or retract the prior output

questions.question: Accumulating panes emit count 8 and later count 10. What should an upsert sink store for that window?
Why is a watermark not proof that no earlier event will arrive?
options: Because it is derived from the slowest input, which may itself be idle
Because it estimates event-time progress rather than guaranteeing it
Because it advances on processing time and ignores the event timestamps
Because it is recomputed per window and resets when a window closes
